facts.claim: Anthropic's Agent Skills docs: unlike a prompt, a skill loads on demand, so you don't repeat the same guidance in every conversation.
Anthropic's Agent Skills docs: loading in stages means only the content a task needs takes up the model's working memory at any given time.
Anthropic's engineering post (October 16, 2025): at startup the agent loads only the name and description of every installed skill into its system prompt.
Anthropic's Agent Skills docs: a skill's name and description are always loaded, about 100 tokens per skill; its instructions load only when it is used, under 5,000 tokens.
The Agent Skills specification recommends keeping a skill's instructions under 5,000 tokens, and its main file under 500 lines.
Anthropic's Agent Skills docs: the description is what Claude matches a request against when deciding whether to use a skill, so it must say what the skill does and when to use it.
The Agent Skills specification gives “Helps with PDFs.” as a poor description; a good one says what the skill does, when to use it, and the words a request would use.
The Agent Skills specification caps a skill's name at 64 characters and its description at 1,024.
Anthropic's Agent Skills docs: a skill's scripts run through bash and only their output enters the context; the script's code never does.
Anthropic's Agent Skills docs: use skills only from trusted sources, because a malicious skill can direct Claude to call tools or run code in ways that don't match its stated purpose.
Anthropic's engineering post (October 16, 2025): when installing a skill from a less-trusted source, thoroughly audit it before use.
Anthropic's skill-authoring guide: Claude uses the description to choose the right skill from potentially 100+ available skills, so it must be specific and include key terms.
Anthropic's skill-authoring guide: for most utility scripts, running them is preferred over reading them; only the script's output uses tokens.
Anthropic's skill-authoring guide lists “Helps with documents”, “Processes data” and “Does stuff with files” as descriptions to avoid.
